newsitem.title: FRANCE: Izetbegovic, Milosevic to meet in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic, Milosevic to meet in Paris.

text.p: Bosnian Moslem President Alija Izetbegovic and President Slobodan Milosevic of Serbia plan to meet in Paris for talks on building peace, perhaps at the end of the week, France said on Sunday.
The Foreign Ministry said France had planned the meeting with Carl Bildt, the chief international civilian representative in Bosnia and played down any role by U.S. mediator Richard Holbrooke.

Holbrooke said earlier in Sarajevo that Izetbegovic and Milosevic were aiming to meet in Paris in about three weeks' time. Bosnia's Serbs, Moslems and Croats voted in their first post-war elections on Saturday.

"This meeting could take place very quickly, if possible at the end of the week, for example," Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said. Paris has frequently been at odds with Washington on policies ranging from Bosnia to Iraq.
Doutriaux said the talks would be "to advance the peace process in former Yugoslavia, to normalise relations between Bosnia and former Yugoslavia."
"We confirm what the French ambassador in Sarajevo, Yves Gaudeul, announced following long-running and regular contacts established by France with Belgrade and Sarajevo," Doutriaux said of the talks.
"The principle of a meeting between Izetbegovic and Milosevic has been agreed in liaison with Carl Bildt," he said, without mentioning any role by Holbrooke.

Before announcing the talks, Holbrooke held separate talks with Izetbegovic and Milosevic in Sarajevo and Belgrade after a U.S. delegation tour of polling stations during Bosnia's first post-war elections.

Speaking after seeing Izetbegovic on his return from a four-hour visit to Belgrade, the American peace architect said the Paris meeting hinged on a resolution of Moslem-Serb disputes over the conduct of the elections.

He was confident the meeting would go ahead. "We said were going to launch an intense diplomatic effort (after the elections). This (Paris meeting) is the first manifestation of that effort," Holbrooke told reporters.
Muhamed Sacirbey, Bosnian ambassador to the United Nations who was with Holbrooke, thanked Holbrooke for his latest round of Balkans diplomacy.
